tagline: Leading personal and commercial insurance provider with digital-first customer experience
hero_kpi_rationale: The Personal Lines segment represents 87% of net premiums in 2025, making it the core business pillar and the primary driver of the company's structural growth.

kpis.name: Personal auto segment revenue share
kpis.explanation: Proportion of net premiums generated by personal auto and recreational vehicle insurance.
kpis.description: The Personal Lines segment is the core of Progressive's business, increasing from 84% in 2023 to 87% in 2025.

kpis.name: Personal auto segment revenue share
kpis.explanation: Proportion of net premiums generated by personal auto and recreational vehicle insurance.
kpis.description: The Personal Lines segment is the core of Progressive's business, increasing from 84% in 2023 to 87% in 2025.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Total amount paid in dividends per share over the fiscal year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD. Source yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Share of net income redistributed. >80% = potentially unsustainable.

kpis.name: Net Premiums Written
kpis.explanation: Total net premiums written by all of PGR's insurance subsidiaries at year-end 2025.
kpis.description: PGR underwrote $83.2 billion in net premiums during 2025, reflecting significant portfolio expansion. This figure also serves as the basis for calculating the regulatory premiums-to-surplus ratio.

kpis.name: Statutory Surplus
kpis.explanation: Total statutory regulatory capital of PGR's insurance subsidiaries at year-end 2025, the basis for the premiums-to-surplus ratio.
kpis.description: Statutory surplus of $28.4 billion at end of 2025 supports premium growth capacity and reassures regulators on PGR's financial strength. It directly conditions the regulatory underwriting limit.

kpis.name: Premiums-to-Surplus Ratio
kpis.explanation: Key regulatory ratio measuring net premiums written relative to statutory surplus; the standard industry limit is 3:1.
kpis.description: At 2.9x end of 2025, PGR sits slightly below the standard sector ceiling of 3:1, indicating residual growth headroom while maintaining regulatory discipline. Two states permit up to 3.5x for PGR's personal auto vehicle subsidiaries.

kpis.name: Non-Insurance Securities Available
kpis.explanation: Value of securities held in a non-insurance subsidiary, available to bolster insurance subsidiaries' capital or support growth.
kpis.description: As of January 31, 2026, PGR held $5.5 billion in securities within a non-insurance subsidiary, constituting a rapidly mobilizable capital reserve to support growth or address exceptional needs.

kpis.name: Hurricane XOL Coverage
kpis.explanation: Excess-of-loss (XOL) reinsurance coverage amount for named storms during the 2026 hurricane season.
kpis.description: PGR renewed its hurricane XOL coverage at $175 million for the 2026 season (May-December), identical to 2025 levels. No losses were ceded under this program in 2025, demonstrating controlled catastrophe loss severity.

risks.title: Underestimation of losses related to climate disasters
risks.score_rationale: Central position in the 10-K, strong language on material impact, upward trend in climate events, critical category for an insurance company.

risks.title: Difficulty pricing accurately due to uncertain data
risks.score_rationale: Repeated and detailed risk, linked to fundamental profitability, mention of data and methodology biases, direct impact on margins.

risks.title: Dependence on unreliable reserve revaluation models
risks.score_rationale: Present as a major risk in reserves, with acknowledgment of structural uncertainties, but mitigated by current practices.

risks.title: Cyberattack or critical system failure
risks.score_rationale: Alarming language on operational consequences, mention of third-party dependency, elevated risk due to system criticality.

risks.title: Regulation threatening use of pricing factors
risks.score_rationale: Explicit threat to business model, with risk of risk segmentation degradation, increasing mentions in reports.

risks.title: Reinsurance shortage or elevated costs
risks.score_rationale: Direct risk to capacity covering catastrophes, dependence on volatile reinsurance market, mention of contractual thresholds and limits.

risks.title: Claims fraud or overestimation
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention in reserves, structural risk in insurance, but mitigated by internal controls.

ai_positioning.summary: Progressive is gradually integrating artificial intelligence into its underwriting, claims management, and customer experience processes, without making it a central communication theme. The focus is on improving operational efficiency rather than disruptive innovation.
evidence: Functional organization including Chief Information Officer and focus on customer service digitalization
Presence of Chief Strategy and Finance Management Officer ensuring technology-strategy alignment
Implicit innovation structure through Customer Relationship Management and Claims organizations
